Extract and Aggregate Raster Values by Polygons

Source: R/extract_by_poly.R
extract_by_poly.Rd

This function extracts raster values within polygon features and aggregates them using a specified summary function (e.g., "mean", "sum", "mode"). It returns the extracted values as a c4e_tbl carrying the raster's context.

Usage

extract_by_poly(
  raster,
  poly,
  fn_agg = NULL,
  na_rm = TRUE,
  pkg = "terra",
  id = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  label = NULL
)

Arguments

raster

A SpatRaster object from the terra package.

poly

A SpatVector or sf object representing polygon features.

fn_agg

A function or character string specifying how to aggregate raster values within each polygon, e.g. "mean", "sum", "mode". Defaults from the kind of variable, else "mean".

na_rm

Logical. If TRUE, NA values in the raster are ignored during aggregation. Default is TRUE.

pkg

Optional character string. The package to use: "terra" or "exactextractr". If NULL, a package is chosen based on polygon count. Default is "terra".

id

Optional name of the column of poly identifying the polygons. When NULL, ID or ID_adm_div is used when present.

weights

NULL, or "coverage" to weight each cell by the fraction of it inside the polygon (uses exactextractr).

label

Optional name shown in progress messages.

Value

A c4e_tbl with the attributes of poly and the aggregated raster values, one row per polygon.

Details

With pkg = "terra", cells whose centre lies in a polygon count fully. With pkg = "exactextractr", or weights = "coverage", each cell counts by the fraction of it inside the polygon, which matters for small polygons and coarse rasters; the computation runs in C++. For other weights, such as population, see extract_weighted_by_poly().

When fn_agg is not given it follows from the kind of variable recorded by read_climate(): the mean for continuous variables, the sum for counts (population) and the most frequent value for categories. The choice is announced.

The raster and the polygons must share a CRS.

See also

extract, exact_extract, extract_weighted_by_poly(), extract_cell_by_poly()

Examples

tmax <- read_climate(
  system.file("extdata", "tmax_daily.tif", package = "c4e"))
#> Read tmax_daily: tmax [K], daily, 2021-01-01 to 2023-12-31, 1095 layers
#> (synthetic).
adm_div <- terra::vect(
  system.file("extdata", "adm_div.gpkg", package = "c4e"))

extract_by_poly(tmax[[1:5]], adm_div)
#> Summarising by polygon with `fn_agg = "mean"`: tmax is a level.
#> # A tibble: 3 × 8
#> # Context:  tmax [K], day, wide; key ID_adm_div
#>   ID_adm_div adm_div_1 adm_div_2  `2021-01-01` `2021-01-02` `2021-01-03`
#>   <chr>      <chr>     <chr>             <dbl>        <dbl>        <dbl>
#> 1 1          West      West A             293.         294.         293.
#> 2 2          East      East South         295.         296.         295.
#> 3 3          East      East North         296.         295.         295.
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: `2021-01-04` <dbl>, `2021-01-05` <dbl>
extract_by_poly(tmax[[1:5]], adm_div, weights = "coverage")
#> Summarising by polygon with `fn_agg = "mean"`: tmax is a level.
#> # A tibble: 3 × 8
#> # Context:  tmax [K], day, wide; key ID_adm_div
#>   ID_adm_div adm_div_1 adm_div_2  `2021-01-01` `2021-01-02` `2021-01-03`
#>   <chr>      <chr>     <chr>             <dbl>        <dbl>        <dbl>
#> 1 1          West      West A             293.         294.         293.
#> 2 2          East      East South         295.         296.         295.
#> 3 3          East      East North         296.         295.         295.
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: `2021-01-04` <dbl>, `2021-01-05` <dbl>
